title: Does modelling the sub-pixel coverage of a moving subject fix the edge ring that burst merging leaves behind?
summary: Follow-up to sensing-ghostring, where no merge or mask fixed the edge ring. Here each frame is a layered mix, a·disc + (1−a)·background, with sub-pixel coverage a from a fitted disc, and the background solved by least squares over the frames. On the same synthetic bursts at 8 frames and 2 px per frame the ring goes from 27.1 dB (aligned plus reject) to 33.1 dB with the disc fitted from the burst itself (large sensor, 4× area: 31.7 dB); at 0.5–1 px per frame it gains 0.4–2.2 dB and stays below the large frame. It is sensitive to geometry: a 0.5 px centre error drops the ring to 25 dB. Stylised: the model assumes the exact shape of the synthetic subject (a flat disc), so this is an upper-bound-style result, not a general deghosting method.
